info.title: Honua Server Management API
info.description: Curated OpenAPI snapshot of key Honua Server administrative endpoints for configuration, import scanning, connections, layers, styles, observability, realtime alert management, durable job viewing, package validation and preview planning, runtime licensing, deploy control, and native client-certificate trust management. For full runtime endpoint discovery, use /api/v1/admin/config and the Control Plane guide.

x-honua-client-certificate-auth.note: OpenAPI 3.0 cannot directly model TLS client-certificate presentation. Required admin/native mTLS modes are enforced before normal RBAC and return application/problem+json with stable client_certificate_* codes.

get.description: DEPRECATED layerId-keyed alias. The canonical style identifier is styleId via GET /ogc/styles/{styleId} (ADR-0048). This alias is kept working for back-compat and returns advisory Deprecation/Sunset response headers; it will be removed only after downstream styleId migration completes. put.description: DEPRECATED layerId-keyed alias. The canonical style identifier is styleId via PUT /ogc/styles/{styleId} (ADR-0048). This alias is kept working for back-compat and returns advisory Deprecation/Sunset response headers; it will be removed only after downstream styleId migration completes. Update the canonical MapLibre style for a layer. Supply mapLibreStyle directly or a GeoServices drawingInfo payload that the engine converts. Optional changedBy and changeSummary populate the layer's revision metadata; changeSummary longer than 1000 characters returns 400. The response includes the persisted style, the incremented styleVersion, the new revisedAt timestamp, and unsupportedSymbolizers[] entries with stable StyleErrorCodes for any symbolizers that could not be losslessly translated. post.description: Scan a supported GeoServer REST or ArcGIS GeoServices REST source and return a deterministic migration inventory artifact. The response body is the artifact itself and is not wrapped in a success/data admin envelope. A 200 response can still carry scanCompleteness.status = failed when the scanner produced an artifact but could not complete discovery cleanly. GeoServer uses that failed-artifact path for transport, timeout, auth-related, and other discovery failures; GeoServices also uses it for auth-related and source-reported ArcGIS discovery errors, while transport and timeout failures still surface as 502/504. Pass the export=json query parameter to receive the artifact as an indented JSON attachment suitable for committing to a migration project repository.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: When set to json, returns the artifact as an indented application/json attachment with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<service-slug>-inventory.json" and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. The slug is derived from the source displayName, sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_-], collapsed, and capped at 64 characters; credentials supplied in the request body are never echoed into the artifact.

200.description: Migration source inventory artifact, including partial or failed completeness states when discovery could not finish cleanly. GeoServer can return a failed artifact for transport, timeout, auth-related, or other discovery failures; GeoServices can return a failed artifact for auth-related and source-reported discovery errors, while transport and timeout failures surface as 502/504. With export=json the same artifact is returned as an indented attachment.

502.description: Failed to connect to source service. This is currently surfaced primarily for GeoServices transport failures; GeoServer transport failures return a failed inventory artifact with HTTP 200.

504.description: Source scan timed out. This is currently surfaced primarily for GeoServices timeout failures; GeoServer timeout failures return a failed inventory artifact with HTTP 200.
